title: Passed pawns: blockade early, if you can arrive in time
outcomes: Names the blockade square in front of a passed pawn
Checks whether the blockader can arrive in time
Predicts win or draw when the defending king is in front or cut off

steps.text:
A **passed pawn** has no enemy pawn in front of it or on the files beside it, so only pieces can stop it. The usual way is a **blockade:** put a piece on the square in front of the pawn. In endings the king is the best blockader.
**Rule of thumb:** blockade early, with a piece that cannot easily be chased away.

steps.caption: White to move. The Black king is far from the pawn.

line.say: The Black king hurries towards it.
The pawn is one step from queening.

claims.statement: Exact result from the tablebase: White wins.

steps.text: The blockade is a strong default, not a duty: it works only if the blockader gets in front of the pawn in time. Ask: **can my blockader reach the square in time, and is it safe there?** In the next pair of positions only Black's king has moved.

steps.title: Same pawn, the king in time or too late
steps.prompt: Only Black's king differs. Does the blockade still hold when the king stands on c8 instead of f8? Predict first, then check.
Before you looked at the exact result: what did you check first, the pawn's rank or the king's distance?
